texts: Moderate aortic regurgitation found during CABG, even without heart-failure symptoms, is best treated by replacing the aortic valve at the same operation.
Guidelines support surgery for moderate regurgitation when the heart is already open for another cardiac operation.
Leaving it risks a redo sternotomy later, past patent grafts, at a much higher risk.
Aortic regurgitation also lets antegrade cardioplegia leak into the ventricle, so it must be dealt with during the operation anyway.
Delayed transcatheter replacement works poorly for regurgitation through a non-calcified valve, and watching with serial echoes only postpones a harder operation.
In the picture, Franky fits new dentures in the orca's mouth while Sanji lays the cabbage in the same open hotel.
Memory hook: one open hotel, two jobs: dentures and cabbage together.
